greek: Αὗται δὲ αἱ γενέσεις Ησαυ (αὐτός ἐστιν Εδωμ)·
hint: A new section: the line of Esau, told the way the line of Ishmael was told at 25:12-18, and with the same opening words.

notes.text: The same opening as 25:12 and 25:19, and as 2:4 and 5:1 before them: αὗται αἱ γενέσεις, the formula that divides Genesis into its sections.
Rahlfs prints the identification in parentheses. Εδωμ is the name 25:30 gives Esau; here it is also the people and the land descended from him, and the morphology keeps the three apart by gender.

reading: [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the origins|the origins, the sources, the productive causes, the beginnings, the manners of birth, the races and descents, the productions and generations, the creations and the created things|γένεσις]] [[name:Ησαυ]]; he is [[name:Εδωμ]].

names.gloss: (Ησαυ, from Hebrew ʿĒśāw, usually connected with śēʿār, "hair", the hairiness of 25:25)
(Εδωμ, from Hebrew ʾĔdôm, which the Hebrew of 25:30 hears in ʾādōm, "red")

greek: Ησαυ δὲ ἔλαβεν γυναῖκας ἑαυτῷ ἀπὸ τῶν θυγατέρων τῶν Χαναναίων, τὴν Αδα θυγατέρα Αιλων τοῦ Χετταίου καὶ τὴν Ελιβεμα θυγατέρα Ανα τοῦ υἱοῦ Σεβεγων τοῦ Ευαίου
hint: Esau's wives. The Hebrew names two of them differently at 26:34, and the difference is a fact about the text, not a fault to repair.

notes.text: Accusative plural without an article: wives, taken from among the Canaanite women.

[[flag]] At 26:34 the wives are Ιουδιν daughter of Βεηρ the Hittite and Βασεμμαθ daughter of Αιλων the Hittite; here Αδα is the daughter of Αιλων and Βασεμμαθ the daughter of Ishmael. The two lists do not agree, in the Greek or in the Hebrew.
[[flag]] The apparatus: ελωμ in A. Rahlfs prints αιλων with the majority.
[[flag]] The apparatus: A writes ελιβεμα at 14, 18 and 41 but ολιβεμα at 2, 5, 18 and 25.

reading: [[name:Ησαυ]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[took|took, received, took hold of and grasped and seized|λαμβάνω]] [[women|women, mistresses and ladies, wives and spouses, mortal women|γυνή]] to himself [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] the daughters [[name:Χαναναίων]], the [[name:Αδα]] daughter [[name:Αιλων]] the [[name:Χετταίου]] and the [[name:Ελιβεμα]] daughter [[name:Ανα]] the son [[name:Σεβεγων]] the [[name:Ευαίου]]

names.gloss: (Χαναναῖος, from Hebrew Kĕnaʿănî, "of Canaan")
(Αδα, from Hebrew ʿĀdâ, usually connected with ʿādâ, "to adorn")
(Αιλων, from Hebrew ʾÊlôn, "terebinth" or "great tree")
(Χετταῖος, the man of Χετ, Heth; Hebrew Ḥittî)
(Ελιβεμα, from Hebrew ʾOholîbāmâ, "tent of the high place")
(Ανα, from Hebrew ʿĂnâ, of uncertain meaning)
(Σεβεγων, from Hebrew Ṣibʿôn, of uncertain meaning)
(Ευαῖος, from Hebrew Ḥiwwî, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ τὴν Βασεμμαθ θυγατέρα Ισμαηλ ἀδελφὴν Ναβαιωθ.
hint: The third wife, from Ishmael's line, which ties Esau back to Abraham's other son.

notes.text: Nebaioth is Ishmael's firstborn at 25:13.

reading: and the [[name:Βασεμμαθ]] daughter [[name:Ισμαηλ]] sister [[name:Ναβαιωθ]].

names.gloss: (Βασεμμαθ, from Hebrew Bāśĕmat, "balsam" or "fragrance")
(Ισμαηλ, from Hebrew Yišmāʿēʾl, "God hears")
(Ναβαιωθ, from Hebrew Nĕbāyôt, of uncertain meaning)

greek: ἔτεκεν δὲ Αδα τῷ Ησαυ τὸν Ελιφας, καὶ Βασεμμαθ ἔτεκεν τὸν Ραγουηλ,
hint: The sons, by mother.

notes.text: Aorist of τίκτω, the verb of bearing a child, used of each mother in turn.

reading: [[brought into the world|brought into the world, brought forth, bore, produced|τίκτω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]] [[name:Αδα]] to the [[name:Ησαυ]] the [[name:Ελιφας]], and [[name:Βασεμμαθ]] [[brought into the world|brought into the world, brought forth, bore, produced|τίκτω]] the [[name:Ραγουηλ]],

names.gloss: (Ελιφας, from Hebrew ʾĔlîpāz, perhaps "my God is fine gold")
(Ραγουηλ, from Hebrew Rĕʿûʾēl, "friend of God")

greek: καὶ Ελιβεμα ἔτεκεν τὸν Ιεους καὶ τὸν Ιεγλομ καὶ τὸν Κορε· οὗτοι υἱοὶ Ησαυ, οἳ ἐγένοντο αὐτῷ ἐν γῇ Χανααν.
hint: Oholibamah's three sons, and the note that all of them were born in Canaan, before the move of the next verses.

notes.text: [[flag]] The apparatus: ιευς in A at 14, ιεουλ at 18. The name is unsteady in the manuscripts.
Where they were born, against the land they leave in 6-8.

reading: and [[name:Ελιβεμα]] [[brought into the world|brought into the world, brought forth, bore, produced|τίκτω]] the [[name:Ιεους]] and the [[name:Ιεγλομ]] and the [[name:Κορε]]; [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] sons [[name:Ησαυ]], who [[came into being|came to be, arose, was brought into existence|γίνομαι]] to him [[in the earth|within, inside of, and by means of the earth, the land, the ground|γῆ]] [[name:Χανααν]].

names.gloss: (Ιεους, from Hebrew Yĕʿûš, perhaps "he helps")
(Ιεγλομ, from Hebrew Yaʿlām, perhaps "he conceals")
(Κορε, from Hebrew Qōraḥ, "bald" or "baldness")
(Χανααν, from Hebrew Kĕnaʿan, of uncertain meaning)

greek: ἔλαβεν δὲ Ησαυ τὰς γυναῖκας αὐτοῦ καὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς καὶ τὰς θυγατέρας καὶ πάντα τὰ σώματα τοῦ οἴκου αὐτοῦ καὶ πάντα τὰ ὑπάρχοντα καὶ πάντα τὰ κτήνη καὶ πάντα, ὅσα ἐκτήσατο καὶ ὅσα περιεποιήσατο ἐν γῇ Χανααν, καὶ ἐπορεύθη ἐκ γῆς Χανααν ἀπὸ προσώπου Ιακωβ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ·
hint: Esau leaves Canaan. The list of what he takes is the same kind of list as Jacob's at 31:18.

notes.text: σῶμα of persons: the bodies of the household, its people counted as it counts its cattle.
The participle of ὑπάρχω used as a noun, as at 12:5: what is at hand, one's substance.
From the face of, the Hebrew idiom for away from a person; the Greek keeps it word for word.

names.gloss: (Ιακωβ, from Hebrew Yaʿăqōb, which the Hebrew of 25:26 hears in ʿāqēb, "heel")

greek: ἦν γὰρ αὐτῶν τὰ ὑπάρχοντα πολλὰ τοῦ οἰκεῖν ἅμα, καὶ οὐκ ἐδύνατο ἡ γῆ τῆς παροικήσεως αὐτῶν φέρειν αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ τοῦ πλήθους τῶν ὑπαρχόντων αὐτῶν.
hint: Why he left: the same reason Abram and Lot parted at 13:6, in almost the same words.

notes.text: 13:6 says it of Abram and Lot: the land could not carry them dwelling together.
παροίκησις, a neighbourhood, and so a sojourning: the land they lived in as neighbours, not as owners.

greek: ᾤκησεν δὲ Ησαυ ἐν τῷ ὄρει Σηιρ (Ησαυ αὐτός ἐστιν Εδωμ).
hint: Where he settled, and the identification repeated from verse 1.

notes.text: Seir is both the mountain and the region; the name is the same word as the Hebrew for hairy, as Esau's is.

names.gloss: (Σηιρ, from Hebrew Śēʿîr, "hairy")

hint: The formula of verse 1 again, now heading the list of chiefs.

notes.text: The formula repeats, marking a second list: verse 1 headed the sons, this heads the chiefs.

hint: The grandsons, named by their mothers as the sons were.

notes.text: [[flag]] The apparatus: αδας in D, αδα in A, and the same again at 12. Rahlfs prints the genitive αδας, a name that declines.

[[flag]] The apparatus: ωμαν in A here, but ωμαρ at 15.

hint: Amalek, born to a concubine, and so set slightly apart from the rest — the people Israel will fight.

notes.text: The Hebrew word here, yēmim, is found nowhere else, and has been read as hot springs, as mules, and as a people. The Greek does not translate it but writes it out as a name, which is its own admission that the translator did not know.

greek: Ταῦτα τὰ ὀνόματα τῶν ἡγεμόνων Ησαυ ἐν ταῖς φυλαῖς αὐτῶν κατὰ τόπον αὐτῶν, ἐν ταῖς χώραις αὐτῶν καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν αὐτῶν· ἡγεμὼν Θαμνα, ἡγεμὼν Γωλα, ἡγεμὼν Ιεθερ,
hint: A third list of chiefs, this one by clan and territory rather than by descent.

notes.lemma: ἐν ταῖς φυλαῖς … κατὰ τόπον … ἐν ταῖς χώραις … ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν
notes.text: Four ways of dividing them, piled up: by tribe, by place, by country, by nation.

greek: ἡγεμὼν Μεγεδιηλ, ἡγεμὼν Ζαφωιμ. οὗτοι ἡγεμόνες Εδωμ ἐν ταῖς κατῳκοδομημέναις ἐν τῇ γῇ τῆς κτήσεως αὐτῶν. Οὗτος Ησαυ πατὴρ Εδωμ.
hint: The chapter closes as it opened, with Esau named father of Edom.

notes.text: A perfect participle used as a noun: the built-up places, the settlements. The verb is found nowhere else in Genesis.
κτῆσις, what has been acquired: the holding, over against the παροίκησις of 7, where they were only neighbours.
